articles.title: The Blood Of Dawnwalker Devs Heard Your 60fps Requests And Have Good News For Console Players
articles.summary: If you wanted to play The Blood of Dawnwalker at 60fps, you'd originally need to get the PC version and hope your rig was up to scratch. Developer Rebel Wolves didn't initially list a 60fps mode for Xbox Series X, PS5, and PS5 Pro when it recently released a quick look at the graphical modes for…
body: "Performance mode was already in the works, but it was still being tested. We simply weren’t ready to promise it yet," Rebel Wolves wrote on its The Blood of Dawnwalker X account. "We heard your feedback. It was clear how much this mattered to many of you, so we focused on finishing the next round of tests. Those results gave us the confidence we needed to confirm Performance Mode for Day one."

Out on September 3, The Blood of Dawnwalker is the debut game from Rebel Wolves, a studio that features several former Witcher and Cyberpunk 2077 developers in its roster, including The Witcher 3 game director Konrad Tomaszkiewicz. Set in a dark medieval world full of vampires and grim fantasy, players will have to grapple with the consequences of their actions as they build up power for a final showdown against the vampire lord Brencis.

"Whether you're talking to your best friend, working to bandage an injured comrade, or battling opponents to save your father's life, when the hunger takes hold, your actions may suddenly be out of your control. Dawnwalker is a game all about making you live with the consequences," Phil Hornshaw wrote in GameSpot's The Blood of Dawnwalker preview.

articles.title: Former Rockstar Dev Calls GTA 6 Leaks 'A Nothing Burger,' Insists Hot Coffee Was Much, Much Worse
articles.summary: As Take-Two works to identify the person or group behind the GTA 6 'CyberLeek' account, one former Rockstar developer has insisted the recent spate of gameplay leaks will have little impact on the success of the game itself.
body: CyberLeek has released 10 GTA 6 gameplay videos and an image of the full map in the space of just six days, sparking a manhunt for the people responsible. Rockstar parent company Take-Two has subpoenaed Microsoft, Discord, and even X / Twitter, but the leaker appears undeterred, and is even running a crypto-fueled poll to determine which video to release next.
All this just a week before Netflix’s timed-exclusive reveal of GTA 6, which is set to fully unveil the game officially for the first time.

From a Take-Two and Rockstar perspective, significant damage is being done. According to Bloomberg, Rockstar still doesn’t know how these leaks happened, nor who is behind them. And while there are no plans to shift this week’s big Netflix reveal, Bloomberg reported that there is frustration and anger internally at recent events, with management sending morale-boosting emails to staff.

Former Rockstar Games technical director Obbe Vermeij, however, downplayed the damage caused by the leaks. Vermeij, who worked at Rockstar North from 1995 to 2009, took to social media to say the Hot Coffee scandal was much more damaging than these GTA 6 leaks.

articles.title: Amid the Blood of Dawnwalker Performance Fears, Rebel Wolves Promises a Day One Console Patch
articles.summary: Promised as a day-one patch, The Blood of Dawnwalker will have a performance mode to target 60 fps on PlayStation 5, PlayStation 5 Pro, and Xbox Series X. This means that console players can choose between quality (30 fps), balanced (40 fps), and performance mode (60 fps) when the game launches on…
body: The announcement is a response to fan backlash; in a now-private YouTube video from Aug. 21, showcasing console footage, developer Rebel Wolves only mentioned The Blood of Dawnwalker 's quality and balanced modes. Although they didn't explicitly state that there would be no 60 fps mode, many fans interpreted the video as such.

Under IGN's version of the console gameplay trailer, which is still online, the top comments range from "It's 2026, 60 fps should be the bare minimum," to "30 fps on a current gen console in 2026 is criminal." It looks like Rebel Wolves took the feedback to heart.

In a social media post on X, Rebel Wolves explains that the team deferred the announcement until they felt confident in their ability to deliver a performance mode on day one. "[It] was already in the works, but it was still being tested. We simply weren’t ready to promise it yet."
Unfortunately, Xbox Series S players won't benefit from this announcement. For them, The Blood of Dawnwalker will be capped at 30 fps.

articles.title: Billie Piper Says She's 'Not the Next Doctor' After That Bizarre Doctor Who Cliffhanger, Asks Fans to 'Chill Out'
articles.summary: Billie Piper has finally discussed her bizarre Doctor Who cliffhanger, and said "everyone needs to chill out and wait" while the show is on hiatus. Piper appeared in the closing seconds of last season following the regeneration of Ncuti Gatwa's Doctor, though exactly who she was playing was left…
body: Speculation around her appearance was fuelled by reports that it was a last-minute addition to the series, amid uncertainty over its future. Indeed, the finale's last third consisted of scenes added in reshoots, as Gatwa had quit the show and required some form of exit sequence.

Now, more than a year on, Doctor Who's future seems no more secure. The BBC has said it will put the franchise's production up for tender, a process in which external companies can bid to make the series. However, several more months have passed since this announcement, and last week Doctor Who writer Mark Gatiss stated that the series' return would "quietly won't happen" as it now needed to be rested.

With all this in mind, it's no wonder that Piper was quizzed about her future in Doctor Who at this weekend's For the Love of Fantasy & Sci-Fi convention in London. And while the actress remained fairly tight-lipped, she did confirm that she was "not the next Doctor" in waiting.

"I am not the next Doctor, I am Rose Tyler in hiatus," Piper said. "Sorry that's a really cryptic answer but because I'm not currently filming Doctor Who as the Doctor I can't lie and say otherwise. I'm sweating, I hate this.

articles.title: Warhammer 40,000 Audiobook Includes AI Training Warning — Read Out by the Narrator
articles.summary: Games Workshop is famously anti-AI, but I was still caught by surprise when the narrator of my new favorite Warhammer 40,000 audiobook read out a warning about training AI systems on the novel itself.
body: AI models training on books without permission has become one of the big topics in the tech space. Last week, a report by 404 Media alleged that Amazon was buying “massive quantities of books, scanning them for AI training data, and destroying them in the process.”

Last summer, it emerged that Anthropic had shredded millions of physical books to train its Claude AI model. The secret initiative, called Project Panama, was unearthed in a lawsuit brought by a group of authors against Anthropic, which eventually agreed to settle for $1.5 billion despite the ruling largely siding with the AI company on fair use.

And in October last year, a federal court advanced two new theories of infringement against ChatGPT-owner OpenAI in a lawsuit brought by authors including Game of Thrones’ George R.R. Martin. No final summary judgment ruling has been issued yet.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Switch 2 physical version is seemingly a code-in-box
articles.summary: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 is the first game in the series to arrive on a Nintendo console since Ghosts on the Wii U in 2013, 13 years ago. The upcoming shooter lands on Switch 2 day-and-date with PC, PlayStation and Xbox.
body: According to independent video game retailer Video Game Plus (via Nintendo Life ), the Switch 2 version of Modern Warfare 4 will be a code-in-box. This means the physical version will simply include a voucher to be redeemed once on the eShop, which locks it to that account and prevents resales.

As a result, the retailer said that it won't be selling the Switch 2 version. "The future of physical gaming should concern every physical game fan," VGP said on X. "And if it's just a box with a download code inside, VGP won't be carrying it. We believe physical games should actually be physical games."

Activision has yet to officially announce the format of the Switch 2 version, but we've reached out to the publisher for comment. It's worth noting that we also don't know whether or not physical copies on PlayStation and Xbox will include a disc at this time.

Should the report be accurate, it would mean that Activision elected not to use Nintendo's Game Key Card system for the Switch 2 version, which bridges the gap between physical and digital by allowing publishers to skip shipping a physical card without preventing players from being able to re-sell their copy.

articles.title: PlayStation Owners Begin Sony Boycott with Digital Blackout Protest
articles.summary: This summer, Sony announced that it would be ceasing PlayStation physical disc production in January 2028. Fans were not pleased with this decision and tried to make their voices heard, to no avail. However, this doesn't mean they're ready to give up either.
body: Various members of the gaming community have been fighting for their rights to own media because, as Sony so kindly pointed out, "virtual content is licensed, not owned." Terminating disc production means that PlayStation owners will no longer actually own the games they purchase or be able to resell them in the future. Digital libraries cause uncertainty. They also destroy the secondhand market, which has always been more affordable for players to acquire games and allows original owners to repurpose games they no longer play.

Companies aren't necessarily open to giving up this all-digital future. Take-Two Interactive, Grand Theft Auto 6 publisher, has been targeted by serious hackers who have threatened to leak the entire game, allegedly as a protest against the lack of physical release for GTA 6. However, Take-Two is taking the matter to court in an attempt to locate the dataminers, all while more leaks continue to surface on social media.

Fans were not pleased with this decision and tried to make their voices heard, to no avail.

articles.title: Hayley Atwell Slams Controversial Captain Carter Scene: 'A Complete Disservice to the Character'
articles.summary: If you thought you hated what happened to Captain Carter in Marvel 's Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness when it debuted in 2022, then take comfort — you're not alone.
body: Speaking at the For the Love of Fantasy & Sci-Fi convention in London, Atwell expressed disappointment with her character's storyline. Peggy Carter has been a significant part of the Marvel Cinematic Universe since her first appearance in 2011 in Captain America: The First Avenger, where she was introduced as one of the founders of S.H.I.E.L.D. and played a prominent role in developing the Super Soldier Serum. However, in Multiverse of Madness, Carter appears as an alternative version of Captain America, donning the recognizable suit and shield and going by the name Captain Carter.

Unlike the original Captain America, Steve Rogers, Captain Carter can't hold her own against the power of the Scarlet Witch (Elizabeth Olsen). She throws her shield, only for the Scarlet Witch to chuck it right back at her, slicing Carter in two.
"If I’m brutally honest, I was so disappointed with how they positioned her and what happened to her in that scene," Atwell said to the audience. "It’s so small, and she gets frisbeed to death.”

articles.title: How to Fish is the latest Steam indie sensation, selling 1 million copies in just two days
articles.summary: If you've browsed the frontpage of Steam in the last few days, you'll no doubt have come across How to Fish, the debut project from developer Dazed Games. The co-op fishing game released on 20th August, and just three days later, its developer announced it had sold 1 million copies.
body: As we've seen with Meccha Chameleon, the Steam post announcing the incredible milestone was brief and to the point, revealing the game had reached 1 million sales in just two days. "Yes, we'll be adding more content! Yes, we'll be fixing bugs!" the developer added.

Despite arriving in close proximity to multiple anticipated releases, such as Mortal Shell 2, the Modern Warfare 4 beta and the Wardogs closed beta, How to Fish has been one of Steam's most played games since it launched, peaking at 268,101 concurrent players (via SteamDB ) - a figure that has grown multiple times since its release day. One thing that likely helped it reach that milestone so quickly is the price, at just £3.96 / $4.95, a 38 percent launch discount available until 27th August.

The game is clearly inspired by more than the recent renaissance of so called friendcore co-op games, as it also makes nods to shooters and other genres. One mechanic rewards you for landing "trick shots", an old Call of Duty community term about landing difficult shots such as no-scopes. It also lets you gamble some of your earned in-game money.

articles.title: A Bizarre $5 Fishing Game Just Sold 1 Million Copies in Two Days on Steam
articles.summary: Following a successful launch weekend, Dazed Games's How to Fish reigns on this week's Top Sellers list on Steam. Friendslop games have become increasingly popular in recent years, as they are affordable, quick to jump into, and provide hours of knee-slapping fun among friends.
body: How to Fish is a relaxing fishing game where you and your friends are tasked with catching and selling fish to upgrade a boat so you can get back home. In this quirky game, players can get inventive when it comes to killing their prey thanks to the wide arsenal of weapons at their disposal, ranging from brass knuckles to SMGs and dynamite. A creature's value increases according to its killscore multiplier, which is based on any impressive trickshots done while killing it.

As players make more money, they'll navigate to islands with progressively harder catches. Even though the game's mechanics are pretty straightforward — cast the fishing line, reel in the creature, execute it, sell it, repeat — some of the bosses can be hard to take down, which is what makes How to Fish challenging as well.

How to Fish has nearly 12,000 reviews on Steam, and it's currently labeled as "Very Positive." It is on sale throughout its launch week, so curious gamers can get it for only $4.95. On Aug. 28, its price will go back up to $7.99.

articles.title: Final Fantasy Resonance is getting a 120-song original soundtrack
articles.summary: Earlier this year, Square Enix announced that we'll be getting our first HD-2D Final Fantasy game in October this year, and it's based on the now-shuttered mobile title Brave Exvius.
body: We've had a few trailers from the game since, and it's certainly looking like it's going to be a massive tite. Now, Square Enix has announced the game is getting a proper soundtrack treatment, with the Final Fantasy Resonance Original Soundtrack will releasing a week after the game comes out (on 28th October), with an OST that spreads over four CDs and 120 tracks.

The soundtrack features music produced by Noriyasu Agematsu, who has created an additional 33 tracks for this soundtrack to complement the 87 that were already released for both Final Fantasy Brave Exvius, and War of the Visions: Final Fantasy Brave Exvius.

There are some absolutely amazing names for some of the tracks (which you can see here), including the likes of "Leviathanomachy", "Wickedness Afoot", "A Bloom in the Gloom of Shadows", "Break the Limit!", "He Who Shoulders Umbral Darkness" and "Overcome the Menace". If you're curious about how the size of this OST compares to other Final Fantasy games, the digital version of Final Fantasy 10 includes 89 tracks, Final Fantasy 7 has 85, and Final Fantasy 8 has 73. So you can expect a lot of music in Resonance, then.
points: Earlier this year, Square Enix announced that we'll be getting our first HD-2D Final Fantasy game in October this year, and it's based on the now-shuttered mobile title Brave Exvius.

articles.title: Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 beta's first weekend numbers are in, and they're good - just not as high as Modern Warfare 2
articles.summary: We're one day away from the end of the first session of the Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 beta, which kicked off Friday. Although Activision has yet to publish any numbers, we can look at its performance on Steam and compare it with other recent Call of Duty betas, as well as those from rival…
body: This initial stage is mainly limited to players who pre-ordered the full game, though free beta codes from content creators, social media giveaways, and other sources have been available if you knew where to look. It's worth keeping that in mind before we begin, as that essentially limits the beta's reach, and could mean larger numbers next weekend when the open portion kicks off.

On Steam, the Modern Warfare 4 beta has amassed a solid peak concurrent of 115,145 players (via SteamDB ). The daily concurrent started out strong on Friday, before dipping with each passing day. Notably, the Modern Warfare 4 beta has its own entry on Steam, and doesn't live under the Call of Duty app.

The full game may yet exist under that app, which would make it harder to track its performance, as the Call of Duty app also includes free-to-play Warzone as well as several of the past years' games.

articles.title: There's a looming GPU supply crisis, which means prices are likely to get a whole lot worse. And it's not just because of memory
articles.summary: A couple weeks back I noted that I'd been tracking GPU prices on an almost weekly basis for a year now, and that things have never been worse. Well, PC Partner—one of the biggest manufacturers of graphics cards you've probably never heard of—suggests it's going to get even worse.
body: PC Partner makes a ton of graphics cards for its consumer facing brands Zotac, Inno3D, and Manli. I've visited one of its main factories in Dongguan, China, and it's production lines are big. So when Singaporean outlet, The Straits Times, notes the company as saying that the supply of graphics cards is going to get real tight in the coming months it's worth listening.

And the worst part about it is that apparently it's going to be the entry level cards that will be the most adversely affected. With severe shortages comes increased prices, and while Nvidia cards with VRAM capacities of 8 GB haven't had the spiking price tags of their more heavily memory'd cousins, it looks like it won't be long before they do.

articles.title: Proposed class action lawsuit against Logitech demands money to be given back to customers after $61 million US tariff refund
articles.summary: A proposed class action lawsuit against Logitech is attempting to recover funds that were allegedly "extracted from American consumers" as a result of the Trump administration's tariffs.
body: The complaint [PDF] is being led by a construction company, SJK Development, and a California resident, both of whom say they bought Logitech mice at higher, tariff-affected prices. It was filed with the US District Court for the Northern District of California, San Jose Division last week (via Ars Technica ).

"This case is an example of a large multinational corporation and its US subsidiary taking advantage of its customers who rely on the integrity of manufacturers to sell products to customers in good faith," the complaint alleges.

"[The defendant] refused to be honest with their customers by raising prices across their product catalog to allegedly account for costs due to tariffs and then failed to return tariff proceeds when the US Supreme Court declared those tariffs unlawful."

While Logitech did not publicly announce price hikes, the complaint makes mention of the company's executives discussing higher prices and profits in regards to offsetting tariffs in its subsequent earnings calls.

videos.title: The Sinking City 2 Video Review
videos.summary: The Sinking City 2 reviewed by Len Hafer on PC, also available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
body: While a lot of the basic mechanics and moment-to-moment survival horror of The Sinking City 2 feel inescapably like off-brand Resident Evil, it's a praiseworthy imitation of its main inspirations. The story presentation shows the limitations of its production qualities at times, and I wish the detective elements were a bit more robust and challenging. But taking on imposing enemies in some truly inspired, detailed, and memorable environments while watching my resources dwindle reminded me of some of the best parts of this entire genre. Nobody really gets a happy ending in the Cthulhu mythos. But I was pretty satisfied with this latest, harrowing peek into its writhing innards.
points: The Sinking City 2 reviewed by Len Hafer on PC, also available on PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X|S.
